 In The Supreme Court Of India

 Sanjeev Kumar Kujur @ Dadu & Ors. App
 Versus
 State Of Chhattisgarh Res
 O R D E R

1. Leave granted.
2.

The present appellants have been convicted for committing offence punishable under Sections 342, 366 and 376(D) of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short IPC) and have been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for ten years, one year and twenty five years respectively, for each of the offence with fine sentence also.
The conviction and sentence has been handed down for committing gang rape of a deaf and dumb women.
3. While entertaining this appeal on 09.09.2025, we issued notice limited to the quantum of sentence and as such in the present order we are not dealing with the merits of the matter.

4. At the time of commission of offence appellant No.1 Reason: Sanjeev Kumar Kujur, appellant No.2 Suraj Das, appellant No.3 Dole @ Mithun Kujur and appellant No.5 Gourishankar were aged about 20  23 years, whereas appellant No.4 Krishna Kumar was aged about 35 years.
They have already suffered incarceration from the date of arrest i.e. on 27.08.2019 and have thus undergone more than six years of jail sentence.
The minimum sentence provided for committing an offence under Section 376(D) of IPC is twenty years, whereas the Trial Court has awarded rigorous imprisonment for a period of 25 years.

5. Considering the age of the appellants at the time of commission of offence and for the fact that three of them appears to be tribal, we are of the considered view that ends of justice would be served Sanjeev Kumar Kujur @ Dadu vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 3 February, 2026
